Subject: Expansion: pricing for new teams / added workloads

Jonas / Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — the Redwood integration for our core chat flows looks solid. Were kicking off an internal plan to expand usage beyond the product team into two more squads (support automation + knowledge search). Before we move forward I need clarity on incremental pricing and how additional usage across new workloads would be handled under your hosted API commit tiers.

Specific asks:
- If we add ~200B tokens/month on top of our current committed baseline, what discount bands apply?
- Can incremental workloads (different API routes / embedding vs. generation) be priced differently, or must they roll into the same per-token pool?
- Do you offer short-term top-ups (monthly) versus multi-month committed add-ons, and how do credits/true-ups work?

I've attached our Q1 usage export so you can see current patterns. Procurement will need a ballpark figure to start internal approval.

Hannah Lopez
Head of Platform
Luna Apps
(hannah.lopez@lunaapps.com)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Expansion: pricing for new teams / added workloads

Hannah — thanks for the clear note and for sending the usage file. I reviewed the CSV and sketched a couple of options that usually fit this pattern. High level: we can support mixed workloads (embeddings + generation) under a single commit, but we commonly model discounts with a blended per-token effective rate and give two paths for expansion.

Option A — Incremental monthly top-up (low commitment):
- Short-term monthly add-ons at a modest discount to list (typically 10–15% off per-token list for large bursts).
- No long-term commit required; ideal for temporary spikes or pilot squads.
- Credits are applied month-over-month; unused top-ups do not roll over.

Option B — Incremental committed add-on (best unit economics):
- Add a committed tranche for the new teams (e.g., +200B tokens / month for 12 months).
- We offer a stepped discount: 20% off list at 200B/month commit, 25% at 400B/month, plus an extra 2–3% for multi-year commits.
- Commit covers all hosted API usage (embeddings + generation) unless you elect to carve out a specific SKU.

Follow-ups I need from you to firm up numbers:
1) Expected % split between embeddings and generation for the added tokens.
2) Whether engineering needs a separate quota isolating support automation.
3) Timeline for when the teams go live (month start).

Ive attached a draft term sheet showing the committed-add-on pricing bands and a simple worked example based on your Q1 traffic. If it helps, we can also run a modeled forecast with your expected split and show monthly cost and marginal unit price.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Subject: Re: Expansion: pricing for new teams / added workloads

Jonas — appreciate the clear options. Procurement is sensitive to both predictability and avoiding overcommit. A couple of points from our side:

- Our engineering org wants a separate quota for the support automation team (security/compliance reasons). Theyd like to ensure support usage cannot cannibalize product generation budget. Is it possible to create per-route quotas within a single committed pool?
- For an initial expansion were leaning toward a 12-month committed add-on but would ask for a mid-year true-up if cross-team adoption exceeds projections.
- Given the volume and our multi-product use, is there flexibility to push the step discount for 200B to 22% rather than 20%? That movement would make the financials much easier for exec approval.

Procurement has also asked for an enterprise-style clause about committed monthly increases (an ability to scale the commitment up with 30 days notice and pricing tiers locked for the remainder of the term).

If you can share a concise proposed price table (showing the current baseline, the +200B scenario at your proposed rate, and the requested 22% scenario) we can take it to budgeting next week.

Thanks — Hannah

Hi Hannah — looping in Rishi (Head of Growth Pricing) to confirm flexibility on the step discount and the commitment scaling clause. Quick answers and a proposal below.

Short answers: yes on per-route quotas (we can enforce per-service or per-key limits), and yes on a 30-day scaled-up commit option with pricing bands locked for the remainder of the term.

Proposal (concise price table):
- Current baseline (as reported): 120B tokens/month (existing commit).
- Expansion scenario: +200B tokens/month committed for 12 months starting 2026-04-01.
- Proposed discount for the 200B add-on: 22% off per-token list (we can offer this as a one-time concession tied to a signed amendment by 2026-03-15).
- Mid-year true-up: permitted once in the 12-month term; overages beyond the true-up are billed at the committed add-on rate.
- Quotas: we will provision a separate API key/quotas for the support automation team; consumption still counts toward the committed total but is restricted by per-key caps.

Next steps:
1) If this looks good, I will generate a short amendment and send it for signature (DocuSign link included).
2) We will provision the separate quota key and share expected rollout docs.

Rishi and I are available for a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the term sheet with procurement if helpful.

Regards,
